group.passage:
Spoons are indispensable eating utensils in our daily lives. Throughout history, spoons have been made of different materials for different purposes, but they typically consist of a small bowl-shaped part with a long handle.
According to archeological discoveries, the invention of spoons can be traced back to 1,000 BC, during which ancient Egyptians are said to have first made spoons out of wood, flint and ivory for ornamental and religious purposes. Back then, spoons, as a symbol of wealth, were in the possession of Egyptian priests and Pharaohs. These ancient Egyptian spoons had elaborate drawings and hieroglyphic descriptions of religious events on their handles and bowls. In ancient Greece and the Roman Empire, spoons were frequently produced with higher value materials like bronze or silver and became more common among upper classes. The earliest mentioning of spoon in England can be traced back to 1259, in King Edward I’s wardrobe accounts. Coronation of every king of England involved the use of special spoons adorned with tiny pearls. Upon the dawn of medieval Europe, spoons were crafted in horns, wood, and brass as a means of eating for both people and animals. Not until the 15th century were wooden spoons replaced by more durable metal ones. Eventually, by the late 1700s, spoons transformed into the modern ones we know today.
In modern times, spoons are not only used for serving or eating food, but they also function as a tool for different tasks. The term “spoonful” is thus created to refer to the amount that a spoon can hold as a standard unit of measure in cooking. A teaspoon holds approximately 5 ml while a tablespoon measures three times the volume of a teaspoon. As for a dessertspoon, it is medium-sized, roughly equivalent to 10 ml. Aside from measuring spoons, dozens of variations of spoons are designed for specific purposes. For example, special spoons are designed exclusively for caviar. They are often made out of wood, gold, or animal horn because silver may change its taste. In essence, the multiple functions and designs of spoons reflect their indispensable role in our lives.

figures.caption: 第3題：四張湯匙線條圖 a–d（2×2 表格排列）
figures.description: 題目下方以 2×2 表格排列四幅黑白線條圖，每格左上角標 a.–d.，每支湯匙有一個英文標註以引線指向湯匙的某部位。a.（左上）：一支細長的華麗湯匙，握柄呈螺旋紋，握柄靠近匙面處鑲有一串圓珠，標註「jewels」指向這些珠飾；匙面為橢圓形，內有鏤空的花葉狀裝飾。b.（右上）：一支以獸角彎曲雕成的湯匙，匙面寬而淺，握柄末端呈動物（鳥／鴨）頭形狀，標註「horn」指向匙身。c.（左下）：一支握柄細長、末端略彎的湯匙，前端為小而深的圓形匙面，標註「bronze」指向握柄。d.（右下）：一支橢圓匙面的湯匙，握柄上刻有一排圖形符號（類似象形文字），握柄末端有雕飾的頭部造型，標註「symbols」指向握柄上的符號。
rows: jewels（握柄鑲珠飾的華麗湯匙）
horn（獸角製、末端為動物頭形的湯匙）
bronze（細長握柄、小圓匙面的湯匙）
symbols（握柄刻有象形符號的湯匙）

questions.stem: What is this passage mainly about?

options.A: Interesting facts about a common utensil.
options.B: Ancient origins of a measuring tool.
options.D: Inspirational stories about a useful invention.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: Spoons were common eating utensils for ancient Egyptians.
options.B: Spoons were viewed as luxurious items before medieval Europe.
options.C: Metal spoons did not come into being until the end of the 18th century.
options.D: Most caviar spoons are made of silver to improve the flavor of the food.

questions.stem: Based on the passage, match each spoon in the following pictures (a ~ d) with its place of origin respectively.

options.A: Roman Empire – medieval Europe – England – ancient Egypt.
options.B: England – ancient Egypt – medieval Europe – Roman Empire.
options.C: medieval Europe – Roman Empire – England – ancient Egypt.
options.D: England – medieval Europe – Roman Empire – ancient Egypt.

questions.stem: Cassandra wants to bake a “spoon cake,” which requires twelve tablespoons of flour. But she only has a dessertspoon at hand. How many dessertspoons of flour should she use to measure the correct quantity according to this recipe?
